nodes.summary: On a finite vertex set, let $S$ be a finite set of unordered pairs of vertices and let $u$, $v$ be vertices. The bridge test of $S$ on the pair $\{u, v\}$ returns true if and only if $u$ and $v$ are not connected by a path in the graph whose edges are the non-loop pairs of $S \setminus \{\{u, v\}\}$.
nodes.title: Characterization of the bridge test

nodes.summary: On a finite vertex set, for a finite set $S$ of unordered pairs of vertices and a pair $e = \{u, v\}$, the bridge test returns true exactly when $u$ and $v$ are not connected by a path in the graph whose edges are the non-loop pairs of $S \setminus \{e\}$. When $e \in S$ is not a loop, this says that $e$ is a bridge of $S$: deleting it disconnects its endpoints.
nodes.title: Bridge test for an edge set

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set and let $ab$ be an edge of $H$. If $a$ and $b$ are not connected in the graph obtained from $H$ by deleting the edge $ab$, then that graph has exactly one more connected component than $H$.
nodes.title: Deleting a bridge adds one component

nodes.summary: The graph of a finite edge set, with decidable adjacency.
nodes.title: Graph of a finite edge set

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set, and let $I$ and $J$ be sets of edges of $G$ that each form an acyclic graph. If $|I| < |J|$, then there is an edge $e \in J$ with $e \notin I$ such that $I \cup \{e\}$ still forms an acyclic graph.
nodes.title: Augmentation property of forests

nodes.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set and a finite set $S$ of unordered pairs of vertices, the forest oracle of $G$ accepts $S$ if and only if $S$ is independent in the graphic matroid of $G$.
nodes.title: The forest oracle decides graphic-matroid independence

nodes.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set, the forest oracle accepts a finite set $S$ of unordered pairs of vertices exactly when every $e \in S$ is an edge of $G$ and passes the bridge test in $S$: its endpoints are not connected in the graph formed by the other pairs of $S$. It serves as the independence oracle of the graphic matroid of $G$, since a graph is a forest if and only if every edge is a bridge.
nodes.title: Forest oracle

nodes.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set, the graphic matroid of $G$ is the matroid on unordered pairs of vertices whose ground set is the edge set of $G$ and whose independent sets are the forests of $G$, that is, the sets of edges of $G$ that form an acyclic graph.
nodes.title: Graphic matroid

nodes.summary: A set $I$ of unordered pairs of vertices is a forest of a simple graph $G$ when every element of $I$ is an edge of $G$ and the graph with edge set $I$ has no cycles.
nodes.title: Forests of a graph

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set and let $L$ be a list of unordered pairs of vertices such that a pair is an edge of $G$ if and only if it occurs in $L$. Then the matroid greedy algorithm run with the forest oracle of $G$ on $L$ returns a base of the graphic matroid of $G$, that is, a maximal forest of $G$.
nodes.title: Kruskal's algorithm returns a maximal forest

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex type $V$. For every list $L$ of unordered pairs of vertices, the matroid greedy algorithm run on $L$ with the forest oracle of $G$ returns a forest of $G$: a set of edges of $G$ without cycles.
nodes.title: Kruskal's algorithm returns a forest

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex type $V$, let $w$ assign a natural number to each unordered pair of vertices, and let $L$ be a list of unordered pairs of vertices in nonincreasing order of $w$ (each entry weighs at least as much as every later one). Let $T$ be the set returned by the matroid greedy algorithm run on $L$ with the forest oracle of $G$. Then every forest $I$ of $G$ all of whose edges occur…
nodes.title: Optimality of Kruskal's algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $V$ be a finite vertex set. For every natural number $n$ and every forest (acyclic simple graph) $F$ on $V$ with exactly $n$ edges, the number of edges of $F$ plus the number of connected components of $F$ equals $|V|$. So a forest on $V$ with $e$ edges has $|V| - e$ connected components.
nodes.title: Edges plus components of a forest

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
